title: This Cuttlefish Sneaks Up on Crabs Using Moving Stripes
subject: broadclub cuttlefish

scenes.text: This predator hides in plain sight with moving stripes.
It's the broadclub cuttlefish, and its prey is the crab.
It rushes toward the crab, then switches on a display of dark stripes running down its head and arms.
Scientists at the University of Bristol called it a new form of motion camouflage.
They put crabs on a treadmill facing screens. The crabs reacted least to stripes moving downward.
The strong motion may overwhelm the crab's vision. By the time it notices, it's too late.

description:
This cuttlefish sneaks up on crabs by moving stripes across its skin.
University of Bristol researchers found broadclub cuttlefish switch on a passing-stripe display near the end of an approach. Crabs tested in the lab reacted least to stripes moving downward, so the display may overwhelm their vision.
What would you do if your skin could change like this?
first_comment: Camouflage or hypnosis: which one is cooler?
